name: scheduling
description: The $scheduling feature: the author-facing surface over the schedule() primitive (spec/semantics/scheduling.md SC11). Mount it on a space or actor to gain one-shot reminders, cancellable deadlines, and a presence-gated tick chain. It exists because two rules in CO16 need a place to be discharged rather than merely stated: arming an unattended (`always`) timer requires wizard authority, so ordinary callers must reach it through catalog-owned verbs; and `tell` is live-only, so scheduled work whose output matters must land durably first. Chains keep no consumer-side state — the pending queue entry is the state, and stopping is cancelling it.

features.description: Feature object carrying the scheduling surface. Verbs are catalog-owned ($wiz), which is what lets an ordinary actor arm an `always` reminder or deadline through them without holding wizard authority itself — the gate is on arming directly, not on the shapes built over it. Internal verbs (_deliver_reminder, _fire_deadline, _tick) refuse any caller but the scheduler.
